query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Earlier studies of other self-lubricating material systems reported low coefficients of friction at 704 °C and favorable friction and wear behavior over broad temperature ranges. However, these results do not resolve the limited understanding of wide-temperature tribological performance in CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys, and effectiveness must be maintained as operating temperature, load, and environment vary. Formulate one hypothesis that identifies a single intervention without presupposing its class, explains its mechanism, predicts friction and wear relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, defines its temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, relates it to prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing approximately 2 wt% Ag into the CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy matrix will promote the in situ formation of a lubricious, Ag-rich tribofilm during sliding, thereby maintaining a low friction coefficient and reduced wear rate from room temperature up to 800 °C compared to the undoped alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy produced via powder metallurgy without Ag doping.
generation.intervention: Modify the alloy composition by incorporating ~2 wt% Ag during the powder metallurgy synthesis of the CoCrFeNi alloy.
generation.conditions: Sliding tribotests conducted in air over a temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C under variable but controlled loads.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation and stabilization of an Ag-rich tribofilm at the sliding interface as a result of Ag segregation during wear.
generation.mechanism: The presence of Ag in the alloy is expected to induce segregation to the wear surface during sliding, where it forms a ductile, low-shear-strength tribofilm. This film acts as a solid lubricant that mitigates adhesive and oxidative wear, thus ensuring improved tribological performance across a wide temperature range.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the undoped CoCrFeNi alloy, the Ag-doped alloy will exhibit a lower coefficient of friction and decreased wear rate throughout the entire tested temperature range, including at elevated temperatures where oxidation and thermal softening are pronounced.
generation.baseline: Tribological performance metrics (friction coefficient and wear rate) of a standard, undoped CoCrFeNi alloy tested under the same sliding conditions.
generation.boundary: The predicted benefits are expected under air atmosphere and controlled load conditions; performance may vary under different environmental settings or load extremes beyond those tested.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative improvement and the stability/dynamics of the Ag-rich tribofilm across the full temperature range need experimental confirmation, and potential interactions with oxide formation at high temperatures remain uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of CoCrFeNi alloy samples via powder metallurgy: one set with ~2 wt% Ag doping and one undoped control set. Conduct a series of pin-on-disk sliding tests across temperatures from room temperature to 800 °C under identical, controlled load conditions in an air environment. After testing, perform surface analyses (e.g., SEM and EDS) to detect the presence and composition of tribofilms.
measurements: Specific wear rate (mm3/Nm) at varying temperatures
Surface morphology and chemical composition (focusing on Ag-rich regions)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Ag-doped alloy does not exhibit a consistent reduction in friction coefficient and wear rate across the temperature range compared to the undoped alloy, or if no distinct Ag-rich tribofilm is observed on the worn surfaces, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

cited_evidence.kind: web:Remarkable wear resistance and wear mechanisms
cited_evidence.text: Figure 3A shows the Vickers hardness and wear rate variations of NiX and Ni3X as the temperature increases from RT to 800 °C. The hardness of NiX and Ni3X gradually decreases from 6.1 GPa and 4.3 GPa at RT to 3.7 GPa and 2.5 GPa at 800 °C, respectively. The high thermal hardness of NiX arises from the solid solution strengthening and the resultant heterostructures [,]. The trend in wear rate of the Ni3X with temperature is similar to that of the conventional alloys. Specifically, its wear rate increases from 1.1 × 10−5 mm3/Nm at RT to 4.2 × 10−5 mm3/Nm at 600 °C, but decreases afterward to 2.4 × 10−5 mm3/Nm at 800 °C. However, the wear rate of the NiX is basically maintained at the order of (10−7 to 10−6) mm3/Nm over the entire test temperature. In particular, it achieves ultra-low wear at RT (1.7 × 10−7 mm3/Nm) and 800 °C (9.1 × 10−7 mm3/Nm). AbstractThe effect and mechanism of grain sizes on the tribological behavior of CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy (HEA) were studied by friction experiments and wear morphology analysis. Under normal low load and low sliding speed, the primary wear mechanism of the HEA samples is adhesive wear. With the increase in sliding speed, the wear mechanisms of the samples are adhesive wear and oxidation wear. The oxide layer formed under the action of friction heat of the coarse grain (CG) sample is easy to break due to the softening of the CG. With the increase of normal load and sliding speed, the wear mechanisms of the HEA samples are mainly adhesive wear, oxidation wear, and plastic deformation. The oxide layer of CG sample has many cracks, and the worn surface also has plastic deformation, which leads to the increase of friction coefficient and specific wear rate and the decrease of wear resistance. Therefore, the fine grain size HEA sample has better wear resistance than the CG sample due to its high surface strength.Keywords: high entropy alloy, grain size, tribological behavior, wear mechanism

chosen.technique: powder metallurgy synthesis with controlled Ag doping
chosen.conditions: sliding tribological tests on CoCrFeNi from room temperature to 800 °C under variable loads in an atmospheric (air) environment
chosen.why: By adding a small amount of silver, the alloy is engineered to develop an in situ lubricious tribofilm through Ag segregation. This intervention directly fills the open question regarding the unexplained wide-temperature tribological behavior of CoCrFeNi alloys by aiming to maintain low friction and wear across the full temperature range. The approach uses well‐established composition-change methods and standard sliding test setups, thereby providing a clear, falsifiable experimental pathway that also aligns with prior results in self-lubricating material systems.
